parallelSafe: Ordering and safety. Each cut edits a distinct banner region of one file plus the shared switch, so parallel worktrees WILL collide on GameServer.ts (imports block 1-170, the constructor 796-1065 where modules/hosts are built, the class field block 611-795, and the handleMessage switch). Safe to run in parallel in separate worktrees (they touch disjoint method ranges and each only adds one constructor line and one import): Cut 4 (auth), Cut 5 (docking/ship edit), Cut 6 (derelicts/person craft), with the merge done sequentially by one integrator and conflicts limited to the constructor and imports. MUST be sequential: Cut 0 then Cut 1 first (they rewrite tick() and handleMessage that everything else registers into), then cut 2 after cut 1; Cut 3 (input and prediction) alone after cut 1 with no other flight-area edits in flight; Cut 7 strictly last, one agent, in its own quiet window, with 7a to 7c sequential. Suggested waves: Wave 1 = Cut 0 and Cut 1 (one agent each, sequential). Wave 2 = Cuts 2, 4, 5, 6 in parallel worktrees, rebased onto Wave 1, merged one at a time. Wave 3 = Cut 3. Wave 4 = Cut 7a, 7b, 7c. Do not start while any other agent is editing GameServer.ts (also true for the P1 registry: it touches the same input lists and systemRows). Sketch of the narrow ServerCtx (net/ServerCtx.ts; implemented by GameServer, ~25 members, getters only plus 4 verbs): readonly gameData, userDB, scene, currentTick, clients (Map<number,ClientConnection> read only); verbs send(ws,msg), broadcastToSystem(systemId,msg), fault(where,e), guard(where,fn); module handles party, trade, market, hangar, quests, codex, achievements, pilots, towing, docking, derelicts, ships (ShipBridge), admin, contrib, sieges, outpost, services, people, arenas (typed as the module classes, already exported from game/*, so no cycles); helpers flying(eid), isDocked(eid), loginPilot(conn, userId), freeBuild(conn), isAdmin flags (everyoneAdmin, guestAdmin). Anything a handler needs beyond that is a smell: add a module method instead of widening ctx. Mark ServerCtx members readonly and keep it in a file with no runtime imports so nothing can form a cycle.
verification: Per cut, before merging: (1) cd server && npx tsc --noEmit (after npm run build:common). (2) npx vitest run server (whole server, slow, forks 6 GB) must be identical in pass count to the pre-cut baseline recorded at the start (record it first; there is an untracked _tmp_join.test.ts to ignore or confirm). (3) Targeted gates: npx vitest run common/src/network server/src/net (replication bit-for-bit, wire-hash pin must NOT change: if protocol.test.ts fails the cut touched the wire), server/src/game/robustness.test.ts safeguards.test.ts players.test.ts (fault isolation, hostile input, join/leave), server/src/game/guestAdmin.test.ts freeBuild.test.ts hangar.test.ts dockingFee.test.ts tow.test.ts social.test.ts for the matching cuts, server/src/ships replay determinism harness. (4) New guard tests added by the cuts themselves: frozen tick-order list (Cut 0); handler-table completeness equals the old switch's case set, taken from git before Cut 1 (Cuts 1 and 2); no file under server/src/net imports ../GameServer (grep test); golden frame-hash test over a 900-tick deterministic LocalTransport session, recorded BEFORE Cut 0 on the unmodified tree and asserted after every cut (this one test catches prediction drift, ordering and snapshot changes at once, so write it first as Cut -1, about 100 lines). (5) For Cut 7: npm run bench:net in server/ before and after (4 pilots, also with --spread), and the tick-time figures from liveStatus/perf metrics in a 40-pilot headless bot run if one exists; reject if per-tick cost rises more than a few percent. (6) Line-count and doc check: after each cut update docs/areas/server-core.md section map and networking.md line references (they cite GameServer line numbers), run the docs link checker. No need to launch browsers; do not use git checkout/stash/reset (project rule: huge uncommitted tree); one commit per cut on a branch so each is bisectable.
suggestedModel: Opus for Cut 3 (input/prediction) and Cut 7 (snapshot hot path) and for designing ServerCtx and the golden frame-hash test: both need judgement about determinism and per-tick allocation. Sonnet for Cuts 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 (structured but mostly mechanical, with module-host design and construction-order reasoning). Haiku only for Cut 2 (verbatim one-line case moves) and doc/line-number updates, with the completeness test as the safety net. Reason: the failure modes of the cheap model (silently weakened coercions, reordered statements) are caught by the tests only if the golden test exists, so the golden test goes to Sonnet or Opus.
tokenEstimate: About 1.3M to 1.9M tokens in total. Per agent: golden frame-hash test about 80k (Sonnet); Cut 0 about 100k; Cut 1 about 150k; Cut 2 about 120k (Haiku, mostly output); Cut 3 about 250k (Opus); Cut 4 about 140k; Cut 5 about 180k; Cut 6 about 200k; Cut 7 about 450k across 7a/7b/7c (Opus); plus roughly 100k of reviewer/integration passes and doc updates. Each agent should read only its slices (60 to 300 lines of GameServer plus its area guide), not the 70k-token whole file; an agent that reads the file whole roughly doubles its cost. Calendar effort is 4 to 6 working days, matching audit section 5 step 3a, if run in the waves above.
hazards: Prediction drift: input application order (drainInputQueue before tick, target-tick ordering, 16 per tick / 64 ahead / 32 waiting caps), the position of recordSelfHashes after replication.endTick, and the shadow stepping in net/Replication.ts must not move; the four hand-written Input.* lists (drainInputQueue, applyInputToEntity, releaseControls, linger close path in connect() ~2830) must be moved verbatim FIRST and deduplicated in a separate PR. Never combine a move with a behavioural change.

Wire format: flags2 of the binary input is full; PROTOCOL_VERSION/PROTOCOL_WIRE_HASH, COMPACT, pilot-row indices (data[0..15], groups from 16, extras after) must not change in any cut. If protocol.test.ts fails, the cut leaked into the wire.

Circular imports: handlers and SnapshotBuilder must import ClientConnection and ServerCtx as type-only from net/ClientConnection.ts and net/ServerCtx.ts, never from GameServer.ts. Modules already follow 'modules never import GameServer'; keep that. Verify with a grep test and with tsc (madge optional).

Concurrent-edit collisions: GameServer.ts is touched by every area (hosts, constructor, switch, systemRows). Other agents adding messages or pilot-row fields during the cuts will conflict; announce a freeze per wave, merge each cut fast, and tell other agents to add new messages to the new handler files after Cut 2 (update CLAUDE.md, server-core.md step 3, and networking.md step 1 in the same PR as Cut 1/2). The constructor (796-1065) and class-field block (611-795) are the highest-conflict regions for parallel cuts. Pending uncommitted work (Burst Strafer/Tow Beam, Repair Beam/Point Defence) must be committed first, and the P1 part registry should wait until after Cut 7 or at least not overlap Cuts 3 and 7.

Per-tick perf: Cut 0 must build the system array once and not allocate per tick; Cut 7 must not introduce per-snapshot closures/objects, interface dispatch in inner loops, or extra Map lookups per entity; keep hot data (queries, spatial grid, dockedShips, personCraft) as direct fields on the owning class. Measure with bench:net and tick ms before/after.

Fault isolation: every handler must still run under guard/try (a throw in any handler or tick system must not stop the tick); async handlers (join/authLogin/authRegister) must keep .catch(fault). Per-client loops in tick (outpost, services, achievements) must keep per-client guard granularity. Also keep the order 'close' guards run in connect() and the Session.loading rule (never save a profile still loading).

Hostile-input validation lives in the switch bodies (Number(msg.id) || 0, String(msg.name), items.slice(0, 80), rate limiter before dispatch, PRE_JOIN pre-join filter, admin-exempt limiter, the chat 'Slow down' reply); moving cases must preserve these verbatim and the registered type set must equal the old case set (add a test, since a forgotten type silently drops).

Shared mutable state moving out: dockedShips, personCraft, wards, inputQueue, interned row keys, fault counts are read from several places (canDamage 1868 and 2269, invulnerable callback 2407, systemRows 5065); expose accessor methods and keep GameServer delegates so call sites are unchanged; do not copy the maps. Construction order in the constructor (Pilots before Quests, ShipBridge hosts that call personCraft.set/delete at ~914-919) must be preserved, and tests build many servers with autoStart:false and flushLazy, so lazy-effect state (LAZY_TYPES, LAZY_TICKS) must travel with the Outbox.

ServerCtx scope creep: it must stay about 25 members (getters, send/broadcast/fault/guard, loginPilot/flying/isDocked); handlers needing more should call a module method, otherwise ctx becomes GameServer under another name and the split gains nothing. SnapshotBuilder uses its own SnapshotHost.

Docs and tests that cite GameServer by line number or method (server-core.md, networking.md, area guides, tests that spy on private methods via `as any`, e.g. robustness/safeguards tests) will break or go stale; grep tests for `(server as any).` and fix with the delegates; update the line map and rerun the docs link check after each cut. Also pre-existing oddities to preserve and not fix in-flight: server/src/game/_tmp_join.test.ts stray test, Brood Mother stub brain, index.ts Fly.io branch.

Process rules from project memory: no git checkout/restore/stash/reset (huge uncommitted tree; commit-per-cut on a branch, and make sure the tree is committed first so each cut is a clean diff); implementing agents must kill any dev servers/browsers they start (one headless browser per agent, none needed here); worktree-isolated agents need common built (npm run build:common) and node_modules linked before tsc/vitest will run.
